newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk sale shrugged off by strong Russian shares.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk sale shrugged off by strong Russian shares.

text.p: Russia's leading share index hit a record close on Tuesday on strong local buying, but metals producer Norilsk Nickel did not move much since the results of its auction came just as the market closed.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed at a record 526.20 after Monday's 518.31. Total market turnover was a strong $67.5 million.
A firm called ZAO Svift, associated with Russia's powerful Uneximbank, won a 38 percent stake in Norilsk in a closely-watched investment tender.
Norilsk shares closed barely changed, with ordinaries at $15.15 after $15.19 on Monday and preferred shares unchanged at $12.50.

"This information (the tender result) came out right before the market close and there really wasn't a knee-jerk reaction -- people are really taking it in (their) stride," said ING Barings chief trader Peter Kizenko.
Uneximbank had been widely expected to win the tender, although doubt had been cast over the sale by Prime Minister Chernomyrdin's eleventh-hour order to suspend the tender.
"I think at this point the news is almost a non-event -- the strategic buying took place beforehand," Kizenko said.

Domestic players were active in most other major stocks, traders said, noting buying in oil company LUKoil, which firmed to $23.90 from $23.25 on Monday, and selling in international long-distance carrier Rostelekom. Rostelekom eased to $4.80 from $4.91.

"Russian investors were visibly active in all the blue chips today," said a Regent European Securities trader. "I do not share their optimism, although for now I do not see any reason for the market to fall. Western investors are showing more interest in selling, but at higher prices."
